legend: Alice and Bob play a game with strings.
Each game starts with Alice choosing a string $$$A$$$ of length $$$n$$$ consisting only of the characters 'H' and 'T' and revealing it to Bob.
The rest of the game is played according to the following procedure, in order:
Bob chooses a string $$$B$$$ of length $$$n$$$ consisting only of the characters 'H' and 'T', such that $$$A \ne B$$$ and reveals the string to Alice.
Now Alice and Bob build a new string $$$S$$$ consisting only of the characters 'H' and 'T'. Bob chooses the first character of $$$S$$$.
Then Alice keeps appending a new character ('H' or 'T') to $$$S$$$ until the game ends.
The game ends immediately when one of the following occurs:
If $$$A$$$ appears as a substring$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ of $$$S$$$, then Alice wins.
If $$$B$$$ appears as a substring of $$$S$$$, then Bob wins.
If the length of $$$S$$$ becomes $$$10^{100}$$$, then Bob wins.
Both players know the rules of the game, and every action is immediately visible to both players.
Now, Alice has already chosen the string $$$A$$$ and revealed it. Given $$$n$$$ and $$$A$$$, determine the winner if both players play optimally from this point onward.

$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A string $$$a$$$ is a substring of a string $$$b$$$ if $$$a$$$ can be obtained from $$$b$$$ by deleting several (possibly zero) characters from the beginning and several (possibly zero) characters from the end.
input: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$)  — the number of games. The description of the games follows.
The first line of each game contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$)  — the length of the strings.
The second line contains the string $$$A$$$ of length $$$n$$$, consisting only of the characters 'H' and 'T'  — Alice's chosen string.
It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all games does not exceed $$$3 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each game, output a single line containing Alice if Alice wins, and Bob otherwise.
note: In the first game, $$$A = {}$$$"HT". Bob can choose $$$B = {}$$$"TH" and set the first character of $$$S$$$ to 'T'. After that, no matter how Alice appends the remaining characters, Bob is guaranteed to win.
